title: Senior Project Manager - Exhibits & Events
description:
The Company:

Czarnowski is one of the four studios of the Czarnowski Collective. It combines operations, strategy, design, and fabrication to create exhibits and events that engage communities, generate brand enthusiasm, and educate consumers. It’s been over 75 years since we opened our doors, but we’re still not resting on our reputation or accolades. We’re wondering “what if...” anticipating what’s next and embracing our role within the Czarnowski Collective as forward-thinkers for forward-thinking brands.

Joining the Czarnowski Collective means the opportunity to be more than a number, more than a job title, more than a spectator. We are a collective of dreamers and thinkers, doers, and makers…and we’re searching for more of the same to join the ranks.

The Purpose:

We’re looking for an experienced Senior Project Manager to lead complex production projects from initial planning and pricing through fabrication and completion. You’ll take ownership of project budgets, timelines, and production execution while partnering closely with account teams, CAD, fabrication, logistics, and outside vendors. If you’re a hands-on problem solver who understands how things are built and can confidently lead projects from start to finish, this is the role for you!

The Job:

  • Partner with Account Directors and Account Managers to develop pricing and establish production requirements for new projects.
  • Take ownership of project budgets, costs, and overall financial accuracy throughout production.
  • Lead project launch meetings and coordinate project execution across account teams, CAD, fabrication, logistics, and other internal departments.
  • Develop and manage project timelines, ensuring key production milestones and deadlines are met.
  • Utilize Czarnowski’s workflow systems to manage project progress and maintain accurate production information.
  • Review and approve CAD drawings for accuracy, constructability, and adherence to project specifications.
  • Oversee production and fabrication, working closely with shop leads and production managers to resolve issues and keep projects moving.
  • Proactively identify risks related to budget, schedule, quality, or production and drive solutions with the appropriate teams.
  • Manage project changes and communicate impacts to scope, budget, and timelines.
  • Coordinate with logistics, outside vendors, and subcontractors to ensure project requirements are met.
  • Serve as a senior production resource and provide guidance to Project Managers and cross-functional team members as needed.

The Person:

  • Minimum 5–7 years of project management experience within the exhibit, event, experiential, or custom fabrication industry.
  • Strong understanding of fabrication methods, including carpentry, metalwork, paint production, tension fabric, and graphic production.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex projects, budgets, production schedules, and multiple priorities.
  • Ability to read and review CAD drawings with an understanding of fabrication and constructability.
  • Strong financial understanding with experience managing project costs, scope changes, and profitability.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to lead and coordinate cross-functional teams.
  • Highly organized with strong attention to detail, problem-solving skills, and the ability to anticipate project challenges.
  • Experience with Microsoft Office and project/workflow management systems.
  • Willingness to travel based on project needs.

  • 401K matching with no vesting period (you are fully vested as of day 1)

title: Senior Hardware Design Engineer (KiCad / PCB / Electronics)
description:
About Gramian

Gramian Consultancy is a boutique consultancy specializing in IT professional services and engineering talent solutions. With a strong background in software engineering and leadership, we help companies build high-performing teams by matching them with professionals who truly fit their needs.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Hardware Design Engineer to develop electronic hardware from product requirements through schematic design, PCB layout, verification, prototype bring-up, and debugging.

The role is highly hands-on and requires strong expertise with KiCad, PCB design, circuit analysis, component selection, verification, and DFM/DFT. Depending on the project, designs may involve digital and high-speed electronics, power, analog and mixed-signal circuits, sensors, communication systems, or RF.

CONTRACT: Contractor engagement, 13 weeks, full-time

LOCATIONS: Remote - Bangladesh, Brazil, Colombia, Egypt, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Nigeria, Turkey

NOTES: Strong hands-on KiCad experience and 8+ years of electronics hardware design experience are required.

Key Responsibilities

  • Translate product requirements into circuit architectures, schematics, and hardware specifications.
  • Develop complete PCB designs using KiCad, including schematic capture, component placement, routing, and multilayer layouts.
  • Select electronic components based on datasheets, ratings, footprints, availability, performance, and compatibility.
  • Prepare and maintain BOMs and alternative component selections.
  • Apply PCB design principles for grounding, power distribution, signal integrity, impedance control, thermal management, and EMI/EMC.
  • Design across digital/high-speed, power, analog, mixed-signal, sensor, communication, or RF domains as required.
  • Perform engineering calculations and validate electrical, thermal, and protection requirements.
  • Run ERC, DRC, netlist, and connectivity checks and resolve design issues.
  • Perform schematic reviews and DFM / DFT assessments.
  • Prepare manufacturing documentation and support prototype bring-up, debugging, and validation.

Requirements

  • 8+ years of hands-on electronics hardware design experience.
  • Strong practical experience with KiCad, including schematic design, PCB layout, routing, design rules, and project management.
  • Strong knowledge of electronics engineering and circuit analysis.
  • Experience translating requirements into working electronic designs.
  • Strong knowledge of PCB design principles, including grounding, power distribution, signal integrity, and manufacturability.
  • Experience with DFM / DFT, component selection, BOM preparation, verification, and debugging.
  • Hands-on experience with ERC, DRC, netlist/connectivity validation, and PCB design reviews.
  • Experience in at least one of the following: digital/high-speed electronics, power electronics, analog/mixed-signal, sensors, communications, or RF.

title: BU22P3 Business Analyst
description:
CAS uses intuitive technology, unparalleled scientific content and unmatched human expertise to help companies create groundbreaking innovations that benefit the world. As the scientific information solutions division of the American Chemical Society, CAS manages the largest curated reservoir of scientific knowledge, and for 119 years, has helped innovators mine, assess and apply that information to keep businesses thriving. The CAS team is global, diverse, endlessly curious and strives to make scientific insights accessible to innovators worldwide.

CAS is currently seeking a Business Analyst. This position will be located in our headquarters in Columbus, Ohio.

Position Summary

The Business Analyst - Scientific Quality Systems supports the design, implementation, and operation of quality management systems across CAS scientific curation service lines. Working under the direction of the Senior Director of Scientific Integrity and in partnership with other business analysts, information scientists, content engineers, and process owners, this role contributes to the buildout and maintenance of measurement frameworks, quality procedures, and analytical processes that ensure the accuracy, consistency, and integrity of curated scientific content.

Key responsibilities include: 1) Support the implementation and maintenance of quality management systems across curation service lines; 2) Compile, organize, and support the analysis of quality review data to identify trends and improvement opportunities; 3) Maintain QMS documentation and ensure consistency across service lines as the system scales; 4) Collaborate with process owners and domain leaders to implement quality procedures and quality improvement efforts within their areas..

Position Accountabilities

  • Quality Management System Implementation — Supports the buildout and maintenance of quality management systems across scientific curation service lines. Maintains QMS documentation including quality procedures, measurement frameworks, and supporting reference documents. Ensures architectural consistency across service lines as the QMS scales to new areas. Applies experience from ISO 9001 implementation to support quality system design and deployment.
  • Measurement Framework Support — Contributes to the design and implementation of measurement frameworks for curation service lines, working within the established architectural pattern of quality dimensions, severity definitions, weighting models, and scoring methodology. Supports the adaptation of existing frameworks to new service lines such as Markush and Physicochemical Properties.
  • Quality Data Compilation & Analysis — Compiles and organizes quality review data from across service lines. Supports trend identification, root cause analysis, and improvement opportunity assessment under the guidance of senior team members. Prepares data summaries and preliminary analyses for quality performance reporting.
  • Process Owner Collaboration — Works directly with process owners and domain leaders to implement quality procedures within their areas. Supports the operational mechanics of quality review processes including scheduling, documentation, and tracking. Communicates quality findings and improvement recommendations in partnership with senior quality team members.
  • Cross-Functional Coordination — Collaborates across curation domains and with cross-functional stakeholders to ensure quality processes are understood, adopted, and consistently applied. Serves as a point of contact for quality system questions and procedural guidance within assigned service lines.
  • Continuous Improvement — Contributes to continuous improvement initiatives by identifying patterns in quality data and proposing process enhancements. Supports the connection between quality findings and operational changes. Participates in improvement projects that enhance the effectiveness of curation quality systems.
  • Documentation & Communication — Maintains accurate and current quality system documentation. Communicates quality process requirements, review schedules, and findings to stakeholders. Prepares materials for Management Review and other quality governance activities.
  • Professional Development — Actively develops analytical, quality methodology, and quality leadership skills through mentoring from senior team members and the external quality systems consultant. Builds knowledge of scientific content domains to strengthen credibility and effectiveness in working with curation teams.

Minimum Education / Experience / Competencies / Knowledge

  • Education — Bachelor's degree in science, engineering, or a related field. Coursework or certification in quality management, quality systems, or a related discipline is desirable.
  • Work Experience — 4 or more years of related experience in quality systems, scientific data operations, content operations, information management, or a related field. Experience with ISO 9001 implementation or quality management system buildout preferred. Experience in business analysis, process documentation, or data analysis is a plus.
  • Quality Systems Knowledge — Demonstrated understanding of quality management system principles and practices. Experience with ISO 9001 or similar quality frameworks preferred. Familiarity with measurement framework design, quality dimensions, and severity/weighting models is desirable.
  • Analytical Skills — Ability to compile, organize, and analyze quality data. Comfortable working with structured data, identifying patterns, and preparing summaries for review. Developing capability in root cause analysis and trend identification.
  • Scientific Acumen — Comfortable working in a scientific content environment. Ability to follow conversations about chemical structure curation, substance data, and scientific content quality without requiring deep subject matter expertise. Not intimidated by the science — able to learn the domain and engage credibly with curators and domain leaders.
  • Communication — Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to document processes clearly, present findings to stakeholders, and work collaboratively with domain experts and cross-functional teams.
  • Learning Agility — Strong ability to learn and apply new concepts, tools, and methodologies. Receptive to coaching and mentoring. Demonstrated ability to grow into new responsibilities and build competency in unfamiliar areas.
  • Technical Knowledge — Proficient with standard business technology applications. Comfortable working with data in spreadsheets and databases. Ability to learn and apply quality management tools and systems.
  • Organization-Wide Perspective — Understands how quality systems support broader organizational goals. Demonstrates awareness of how curation quality connects to CAS products, services, and customer outcomes.

CAS offers a competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package, including a generous vacation plan, medical, dental, vision insurance plans, and employee savings and retirement plans. Candidates for this position must be authorized to work in the United States and not require work authorization sponsorship by our company for this position now or in the future. title: Postdoctoral Researcher in Experimental Memory for Circular Battery Materials
description:
Are you excited by the challenge of turning large, heterogeneous analytical datasets into reusable chemical knowledge? Do you want to combine spectroscopy, data science, and industrial production data to accelerate circular battery-material innovation? Then join us in developing experimental memory for sodium-ion battery materials.

Join our team!

We are looking for a Postdoctoral Researcher to play a central role in CONTINUUM, a project that transforms heterogeneous analytical and process data into persistent experimental memory. You will develop and validate methods that connect NMR and IR spectra with sample, batch, process, and performance information, making it possible to recover relevant precedents, trends, deviations, and overlooked results. You will work in the Slootweg Group at the Van 't Hoff Institute for Molecular Sciences in close collaboration with industrial partner BOR-LYTE and with data-science expertise at the University of Amsterdam.
This position offers a unique opportunity to combine analytical chemistry, scientific data engineering, statistics, and machine learning in a framework that supports faster interpretation of production variability and qualification of alternative or circular raw-material inputs for sodium-ion battery materials.

This is what you are going to do
  • Define the CONTINUUM data architecture, metadata, and provenance requirements.
  • Develop traceable pipelines to ingest, quality-control, and harmonise large NMR and IR datasets.
  • Benchmark spectral retrieval, multivariate, clustering, and machine-learning methods.
  • Build a demonstrator linking analytical features to sample, batch, process, and performance context.
  • Validate the framework with BOR-LYTE's production data and publish the results.

This is what we ask of you
  • With large, imperfect datasets, you preserve provenance and distinguish evidence from tentative correlations.
  • You communicate clearly across chemistry, data science, and industrial production.
  • You develop reproducible, well-documented data-processing and analysis methods.
  • You work and think at doctoral level in chemistry, data science, chemometrics, or a related field.
  • You have hands-on experience with scientific programming, preferably Python, and complex research data.
  • You have experience with NMR or IR, chemometrics, data engineering, information retrieval, or machine learning.
  • FAIR data, battery materials, production data, or industrial experience is beneficial but not required.

This is what we offer you
You will work in CONTINUUM at the interface of analytical chemistry, data science, high-tech manufacturing, and the circular economy. Methods developed at the University of Amsterdam will be validated in BOR-LYTE's sodium-ion conducting-salt production environment.

You will gain:

Experience combining analytical chemistry with data pipelines, statistics, and machine learning;

Direct collaboration on real industrial production and quality-control challenges;

Opportunities to develop scientific, software, and translational skills.

We offer a temporary employment contract for 38 hours per week for a period of 18 months, corresponding to the planned duration of the CONTINUUM project. The preferred starting date is 1st of December 2026.

The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and dependent on relevant experience, ranges between € 3,706 - € 5,760 (scale 10). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile Researcher 4 is applicable. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants. The Collective Labour Agreement of Dutch Universities is applicable.

Besides the salary and a vibrant and challenging environment at Science Park we offer you multiple fringe benefits:
  • 232 holiday hours per year (based on fulltime) and extra holidays between Christmas and 1 January;
  • multiple courses to follow from our Teaching and Learning Centre;
  • multiple courses on topics such as leadership for academic staff;
  • multiple courses on topics such as time management, handling stress and an online learning platform with 100+ different courses;
  • 7 weeks birth leave (partner leave) with 100% salary;
  • partly paid parental leave;
  • a pension at ABP for which UvA pays two third part of the contribution.

Are you curious to read more about our extensive package of secondary employment benefits, take a look here.

This is where you will work
You will join the Slootweg Group within the Synthesis & Catalysis / Sustainable Chemistry theme at HIMS. Our group focuses on circular chemistry, sustainable main-group chemistry, and the development of scalable and data-driven chemical processes.

Within CONTINUUM, you will work at the interface of analytical chemistry and data science, developing methods that reconstruct heterogeneous NMR, IR, process, and performance data into reusable experimental memory.

The project addresses a central challenge in circular manufacturing: using accumulated production evidence to understand process and batch variability and to qualify more variable alternative or secondary raw-material inputs.

You will collaborate closely with BOR-LYTE and with the data-science experts at the University of Amsterdam. Research is performed primarily at the University, while industrial validation uses BOR-LYTE's production environment and datasets.

The Van 't Hoff Institute for Molecular Sciences (HIMS) is one of eight institutes of the University of Amsterdam (UvA) Faculty of Science. HIMS performs internationally recognized chemistry and molecular research, curiosity driven as well as application driven. This is done in close cooperation with the chemical, flavor & food, medical and high-tech industries. Research is organized into four themes: Analytical Chemistry, Computational Chemistry, Synthesis & Catalysis and Molecular Photonics.

The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain.

If you recognize yourself in the profile and are interested in the position, we look forward to receiving your motivation letter and CV. You can respond via the red button up to and including November 15, 2026.
Please include the following documents in your application (as PDF files):
  • A motivation letter (max. 2 pages A4).
  • Your CV, including the months (not just years) when referring to your education and work experience, including a list of publications.
  • Contact details of at least one academic reference.

We will review applications on a rolling basis and continue recruiting until the position is filled. In the event of equal suitability, preference will be given to the internal candidate.

A knowledge security check can be part of the selection procedure (for details: national knowledge security guidelines). If you receive an error message while applying from abroad, please try again later or contact us for assistance.

prof.dr. J.C. Slootweg, j.c.slootweg@uva.nl

Open Hours: 
Part-time: Monday – Thursday 4:00pm - 8:00pm – Some weekends

Essential Job Functions include but are not limited to; Registration functions that vary by location and/or department. Functions may include the following:

  • Maintains all admission accuracy system errors and warnings by the end of the shift. This also includes running all insurance eligibility on all appropriate admissions.
  • Scans documents into general scanning software.
  • Must be able to perform the physical demands of the job.
  • Maintains regular and reliable attendance.
  • Checks all outpatient orders for accuracy and gives to OP Orders Coordinator before checking inpatient. Also, make a copy of the order for the OP Order Coordinator if the provider is not in the EMR system.

  • Collects patient’s demographics and necessary signatures.

  • Maintains accurate petty cash balances daily.

title: Technician - Motion Solutions: Hydraulic
description:
The Hydraulic Technician is responsible for inspecting, troubleshooting, repairing, rebuilding, testing, and documenting hydraulic components and systems, including hydraulic and pneumatic cylinders, pumps, motors, valves, power units, PTOs, and related fluid power equipment. This role requires strong mechanical aptitude, hydraulic product knowledge, safe work practices, and the ability to diagnose equipment failures, identify required parts, complete quality repairs, and support customer needs in a shop or field service environment.

Salary: $30 - $34 an hour | DOE

Primary Duties:

  • Inspect, troubleshoot, repair, rebuild, assemble, and test hydraulic and pneumatic cylinders, hydraulic pumps, motors, valves, DC power units, PTOs, high-pressure components, and related hydraulic equipment.
  • Evaluate equipment condition, determine probable cause of failure, identify required parts, prepare labor estimates, and complete repairs accurately and timely.
  • Read and interpret hydraulic schematics, work orders, technical specifications, parts diagrams, service manuals, and related documentation to support diagnosis and repair.
  • Disassemble, clean, measure, inspect, and reassemble hydraulic components using appropriate tools, measuring devices, test equipment, and shop procedures.
  • Perform functional testing, pressure testing, leak testing, and quality checks to verify safe and reliable equipment operation before return to service.
  • Document work performed, parts used, inspection findings, test results, and repair recommendations in accordance with company procedures.
  • Maintain, organize, and care for tools, equipment, work areas, and inventory used in hydraulic repair and service activities.
  • Assist with field service work, customer technical support, installations, troubleshooting, or onsite repairs as needed.
  • Coordinate with sales, customer service, purchasing, operations, and other departments to support timely repair completion and customer satisfaction.
  • Follow all safety, quality, environmental, and shop procedures, including proper lockout/tagout practices, pressure safety precautions, PPE requirements, and safe handling of hydraulic fluids and components.
  • Develop, maintain, and share hydraulic product knowledge and provide technical support or informal guidance to coworkers as appropriate.
  • Address customer requests, concerns, and repair-related questions professionally, using a positive, solution-oriented approach.
  • A level III may provide informal guidance, coaching, or mentoring to less experienced team members on standard assembly practices and procedures.

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Education & Work Experience

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; technical school, vocational training, fluid power, hydraulic systems, diesel, mechanical, industrial maintenance, or related skilled trades coursework preferred.
  • Requires 2–4 years of related hydraulic repair, fluid power, mechanical repair, industrial maintenance, equipment service, or shop technician experience; level may vary based on demonstrated knowledge and experience.
  • Experience repairing or rebuilding hydraulic cylinders, pumps, motors, valves, power units, PTOs, or related fluid power components preferred.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Solid working knowledge of hydraulic and pneumatic principles, fluid power components, hydraulic circuits, seals, fittings, hoses, cylinders, pumps, motors, valves, power units, and related repair practices.
  • Ability to troubleshoot hydraulic systems and components, identify failure causes, determine repair requirements, and recommend appropriate corrective actions.
  • Ability to read, interpret, and follow hydraulic schematics, parts diagrams, service manuals, work orders, technical instructions, and inspection or testing documentation.
  • Ability to safely use hand tools, power tools, measuring instruments, diagnostic tools, test stands, lifting equipment, and standard shop equipment used in hydraulic repair and maintenance.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude, attention to detail, manual dexterity, hand-eye coordination, and ability to perform precise inspection, assembly, measurement, and testing activities.
  • Basic math skills and ability to verify measurements, dimensions, tolerances, clearances, pressure ratings, and component fit using appropriate tools and references.
  • Ability to identify quality or performance issues, make routine adjustments, complete repairs accurately, and escalate complex technical concerns when needed.
  • Ability to communicate effectively, collaborate with coworkers and other departments, and interact professionally with internal and external customers.
  • Ability to prioritize assigned work, meet deadlines, complete documentation accurately, maintain clean and organized work areas, and support reliable onsite attendance.
  • May demonstrate leadership skills by providing informal guidance, coaching, or mentoring to less experienced employees on hydraulic repair practices and standard work procedures.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

  • Work is performed primarily in a production, electrical assembly, panel building, pneumatic assembly, testing, and shop environment with exposure to electrical components, wiring, tools, moving equipment, shop noise, sharp materials, production equipment, test stands, and pressurized systems.
  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, reach, climb, crouch, kneel, and use hands and arms for extended periods while performing wiring, assembly, inspection, testing, troubleshooting, documentation, and production support activities.
  • Ability to lift, carry, push, or pull up to 70 pounds, with assistance or mechanical lifting devices as appropriate.
  • Frequent use of hand tools, power tools, wiring tools, measuring instruments, diagnostic equipment, computers, and standard office equipment.
  • Use of required personal protective equipment and adherence to applicable safety, quality, electrical assembly, and production procedures is required.
  • Onsite regular and reliable attendance is required.
  • Up to 10% travel as needed by land or air.

Additional Information:

MFCP Participates in E-Verify

We do not discriminate on the basis of age, race, sex, color, religion, national origin, marital status, sexual orientation, veteran status, military status, disability, genetic information, or any other applicable status protected by federal, state or local law."

Candidates are subject to pre-employment criminal background, drug screen, and DMV record review, along with reference checks.

  • Strong understanding of coding accuracy, medical necessity, and clinical validation.

title: Infrastructure Engineer/Architect
description:
Resource Management Concepts, Inc. (RMC) provides high-quality, professional services to government and commercial sectors. Our mission is to deliver exceptional management and technology solutions supporting the protection and preservation of the people and environment of the United States of America.

RMC is seeking a Denied, Disrupted, Intermittent, and Limited (DDIL) Subject Matter Expert to guide strategy and architecture for secure mission services operating under constrained connectivity. This role focuses on operating at the intersection of tactical communications, systems engineering, and advanced cybersecurity, this role addresses the unique technical challenges of enforcing Zero Trust principles (continuous verification, least privilege access, explicit risk-based attestation) when continuous reachback to enterprise identity providers, policy engines, and cloud trust brokers is degraded or entirely severed. The engineer will establish resilient Policy Enforcement Points (PEP) and decentralized Policy Decision Points (PDP), architect edge-capable Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) solutions, and optimize cryptographic overhead across constrained tactical data links.

We are looking for someone who has designed, evaluated, or fielded systems for these conditions and understands the tradeoffs involved. The SME will help Government stakeholders and engineering teams determine which capabilities must operate locally, what information can be cached or replicated, how long that information remains trustworthy, and how systems reconnect safely. Success requires sound technical judgment grounded in mission needs and experience beyond traditional enterprise availability planning.

This position is contingent on contract award and position availability. It is a full-time, on-site role at a Government facility in Charleston, SC.

What You’ll Do:

  • Develop DDIL strategies, architectural approaches, and implementation roadmaps for mission applications and supporting security services.
  • Work with mission owners to define operational scenarios, connectivity constraints, mission priorities, and acceptable levels of degraded service.
  • Translate those scenarios into requirements for local autonomy, bandwidth use, latency, outage duration, synchronization, and recovery.
  • Define which identity, authorization, directory, credential, and data protection capabilities must remain available without enterprise reach back.
  • Architect local identity and attribute services, including virtual directories and approved caching of security information.
  • Establish approaches for cached attribute freshness, credential expiration, revocation awareness, authorization policy updates, and operation when authoritative sources cannot be reached.
  • Evaluate access control tradeoffs, including when services should deny access, permit bounded local operation, or require additional safeguards.
  • Design synchronization and reconnection approaches that address conflicting updates, stale identity data, audit records, and restoration of enterprise consistency.
  • Define dependencies among applications, identity providers, policy services, directories, encryption services, and key management infrastructure.
  • Assess data placement, replication, and protection requirements across connected and disconnected environments, including approved cross-domain interfaces.
  • Develop architecture diagrams, interface requirements, alternatives analyses, risk assessments, and phased implementation recommendations.
  • Support agreements and approval documentation governing the caching and use of identity and security attributes.
  • Guide prototypes and demonstrations that validate architectural assumptions under representative network impairments.
  • Define measurable acceptance criteria and help teams evaluate mission continuity, security behavior, and recovery during connectivity loss and restoration.
  • Coordinate with Government stakeholders, mission partners, security personnel, and engineering teams to resolve architectural gaps and guide implementation.

Requirements

  • Active TS/SCI clearance with the ability to obtain a CI polygraph.
  • Expertise designing, evaluating, or fielding systems for denied, disrupted, intermittent, or limited connectivity (DDIL).
  • Experience architecting disconnected operations, local processing, and eventual synchronization.
  • Ability to translate operational constraints into requirements, architecture decisions, and testable performance criteria.
  • Knowledge of distributed systems, including consistency, replication, caching, conflict resolution, and recovery.
  • Experience managing offline identity, authentication, authorization, and credential dependencies.
  • Understanding of risks from stale attributes, delayed revocations, expired credentials, and unavailable policy/key services.
  • Ability to assess bandwidth, latency, packet loss, and availability impacts.
  • Experience developing technical strategies, architecture documentation, alternatives analyses, and roadmaps.
  • Ability to explain tradeoffs and risks to Government leaders and guide multidisciplinary engineering teams.
  • Experience deploying local PEPs and lightweight PDPs on edge appliances and dismounted kits.
  • Experience with modeling, simulation, and HWIL testing of tactical link degradation, EW effects, and packet loss.

Desired Skills

  • Intelligence Community experience.
  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree.
  • Operational experience in tactical, deployed, expeditionary, or edge environments.
  • ICAM, virtual directories, federation, and local identity/attribute caching.
  • Attribute-based access control, local enforcement, bounded offline access, and policy synchronization.
  • TDF, data tagging, encryption, and disconnected access enforcement.
  • Disconnected PKI, certificate validation, credential renewal, and key availability.
  • Store-and-forward messaging, durable queues, retries, duplicate handling, and reconnection reconciliation.
  • Approved cross-domain and mission-partner identity/data exchanges.
  • AWS, Kubernetes, OpenShift, and enterprise-to-edge deployments.
  • Network impairment testing, fault injection, and degraded-mode demonstrations.
  • Zero Trust controls adapted for intermittent connectivity.
  • Software-defined microsegmentation, overlay networks, and dynamic perimeters across tactical transports, including HF/VHF/UHF, SATCOM, mesh, and 5G.

Benefits

At RMC, we're committed to your career growth! RMC differentiates itself from other firms through its investment in our employees. We invest our resources to train, certify, educate, and build our employees.

RMC can offer you a great place to work with a small company feel and give you the experience, tuition assistance, and certifications that will take your career to the next level. This also includes a competitive paid vacation package with 11 paid federal holidays. Additionally, we also offer high-quality, low-deductible healthcare plans, pet insurance, and a competitive 401K package.

Salary at RMC is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, a candidate's specific combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific requirements.

title: MASTER TECHNICIAN
description:
Master Technician — $50–$55/Flag Hour, 90-Day Full-Rate Guarantee

Jim Taylor Auto Group — Monroe (Buick GMC) · Ruston (Ford Lincoln) · Rayville (Chevrolet)

We're hiring Master-level technicians at all three of our stores. If you're a certified tech who's tired of fighting for hours, watching the diagnostic work go to someone with less certification than you, or seeing your pay plan change every time a new manager shows up, read on. If you don't hold a current factory Master-level certification, this isn't the right posting; we have other technician openings.

Pay, in plain terms

$50–$55 per flag hour, set by your certification level (GM Master / World Class or Ford Senior Master). Your first 90 days are guaranteed at 40 hours a week at your full rate while you learn our shop and build your book. That's a $2,000–$2,200 weekly floor from day one, and the pay plan is written down before you start. After 90 days you're on straight flat rate, with no cap on what you can flag.

What the work looks like

You get the drivability, electrical, and heavy-line tickets your certification earns. Dispatch is run by a person, not a free-for-all, and the job is to keep your bay loaded with the work you're best at. Late-model GM and Ford product, healthy warranty and customer-pay mix, parts departments that stock for the shop instead of against it.

Who this is for

Current GM Master / World Class or Ford Senior Master certification. Five-plus years dealership flat-rate experience. You're comfortable on flat rate and know how to flag your hours. You get paid for what you produce, and you like it that way. Your own tools, a clean insurable driving record, and the ability to diagnose instead of throwing parts. ASE Master is a plus.

Who this is not for

We've built a shop where the techs help each other and nobody's above pulling a buddy out of a hole. If you keep your knowledge to yourself, treat advisors and porters like the help, or need drama to feel busy, you won't like it here and we won't pretend otherwise. We hire for attitude as hard as we hire for skill.

How we operate

People DRIVE Us isn't a wall poster; it's the rubric we review on. Dedication means staying on a job until it's fixed right. Responsibility means owning your work, your comebacks, and your word. Initiative means you don't wait to be told. Value means you recommend what the customer needs and nothing they don't. Empathy means you treat the lube tech the way you'd want to be treated at 22.

What Jim Taylor offers

Medical, dental, and vision; disability and life insurance; 401(k) with employer match. Free CorMedical Clinic access, including doctor visits, mental health, physical therapy, and dietitian services at no cost. Paid vacation, sick time, and five paid holidays. Paid OEM certification and ASE support. Employee pricing on vehicles, parts, and service, plus referral bonuses. A structured first 90 days with an assigned mentor. A three-generation, family-owned group that's served Northeast Louisiana for more than 20 years and promotes from within.

Apply

Apply here, or stop by any of our stores and ask for the Service Manager. Currently employed techs are welcome and your inquiry stays confidential. We move fast with the right person.

Jim Taylor Auto Group is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind.

This position is also responsible for ensuring that annual re-assessments are completed in a strengths-based, client-centered manner and that the assessment and treatment plan are shared with the multi-disciplinary team working with the client.

The successful candidate will have a degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics, physics, or a related field and a strong interest in modeling, simulation, and/or software development.

The systems modeling, analysis, and research technology group develops modeling and simulation software and other tools to support analysis of military systems, including weapons systems, communications systems, and other systems that support national defense. We develop models and conduct simulations over a broad range of spatial and temporal scales using a variety of approaches to support customer objectives. As a member of the team, you will apply your software development and/or engineering/science skills daily to develop creative solutions to challenging problems.

We are a research team, and the application and nature of our work can vary. You will be continuously challenged to learn and grow expertise in new areas. The most successful candidate will have a strong technical background in science, engineering, applied physics, computer science, or mathematics and a desire to continue expanding their knowledge. Experience (and desire!) in writing robust and performant software is also highly desirable. If this describes you, please apply!

If offered this position, you will be an occasional employee, which is an hourly, non-exempt position. As an occasional employee, you are not benefits eligible and hours worked are dependent on the level of support needed. Hours of support needed will be determined by supervisor and/or project manager. For the Arlington office, we are relocating to the Alexandria, VA area in early 2027.

Salary Range: $72K - $121K

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Work closely with multidisciplinary science and engineering teams to develop innovative approaches in representing the structure and behavior of systems.
  • Review literature and report findings to support collaborative solution development.
  • Present candidate solutions to colleagues and adjust designs based on feedback.
  • Contribute to the development of technical reports and other modes of communication of technical work.
  • Occasionally work independently to learn about various classes of military systems to support model development.

Position Requirements:

The nature of work requires the eligibility to apply for and hold a US security clearance. Selected applicants will undergo a security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements at the time of employment. You are a qualified candidate if you have the following.

  • A BS or higher in Computer Science, Engineering, Physics, or Mathematics.
  • 0-2 years of relevant work experience.
  • U.S. Citizenship Required with the ability to obtain a clearance.
  • Experience writing code and developing software.
  • A strong interest in solving complex challenges.

Position Preferred Qualifications:

Above all, we value passion, a continuous desire to learn, and teamwork. We are confident that if you possess the right attitude, work ethic, and skill set, you will succeed in the role. In addition to the experience and skills above, if you have any of the following, you will be able to accelerate your effectiveness and impact.

  • A graduate degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Physics, or Mathematics.
  • A desire to work in a dynamic team environment.
  • Ability to communicate effectively through verbal and written mediums with technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Familiarity with artificial intelligence, systems science, systems theory, and/or modeling and simulation theory.
  • Familiarity with software architecture, algorithms, data structures, design patterns, API design, and/or test-driven development.

COMPANY INFORMATION:

Applied Research Associates, Inc. is an employee-owned international research and engineering company recognized for providing technically superior solutions to complex and challenging problems in the physical sciences. The company, founded in Albuquerque, NM, in 1979, currently employs over 2,176 professionals and continues to grow. ARA offices throughout the United States and Canada provide a broad range of technical expertise in defense technologies, civil technologies, computer software and simulation, systems analysis, environmental technologies, and testing and measurement. The corporation also provides sophisticated technical products for environmental site characterization, pavement analysis, and robotics.

At ARA, employees are our greatest assets. The corporation realizes that employee ownership fosters greater creativity and initiative along with higher performance and customer satisfaction levels. ARA gives employees the tools, training, and opportunities to take more active roles as owners. The culture is challenging; innovation and experimentation are the norm. Employees are eligible for contributions which not only add to the company’s success, but also their own through the Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP). The motto, “Engineering and Science for Fun and Profit” sums up the ARA experience. For additional information and an opportunity to join this unique workplace, please apply at careers.ara.com.

title: Seasonal HR Associate | Compensation & Rewards
description:
Seasonal HR Associate – Compensation & Benefits

GENERAL DESCRIPTION


The Seasonal HR Associate – Compensation & Benefits provides operational and administrative support to the Compensation & Rewards team. The role processes and documents approved compensation and personnel actions, administers request intake and HR ticketing workflows, maintains compensation and job data, and coordinates timely service across HR partners.


The position monitors service levels, supports data integrity, audit and compliance activities, system testing, performance-process administration, reporting, and process documentation. It operates within established procedures and approval authorities, escalating matters that require policy interpretation, compensation analysis, benefit eligibility decisions, or management approval.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Compensation Actions, Incentives and Allowances

  • Register, document, process and communicate approved compensation actions, including promotions, salary adjustments, market adjustments, job changes, transfers, reclassifications and other employee actions.\
  • Support the administration and recordkeeping of approved functional incentives, supplemental and referral bonuses, and car, cellular or other allowances.
  • Review supporting documents for completeness, effective dates and required approvals; validate employee, position, organizational, salary and cost-center data before processing in SAP or other applicable HR systems.
  • Confirm completion or discrepancies to the requesting partner and maintain accurate logs, approvals, corrections and follow-up evidence.
  • Coordinate permitted retroactive transactions and payroll-calendar dependencies with Payroll and other partners.

JIRA Administration, Intake Governance and HR Ticketing

  • Monitor JIRA and other HR ticketing channels daily; triage, categorize, acknowledge, assign and route requests consistently against defined acceptance criteria and due process.
  • Monitor turnaround time and SLA compliance, identify items nearing breach, flag urgent or overdue cases, and help unblock stalled workflows and approvals.
  • Maintain system hygiene by validating labels, fields, ownership, required documentation and ticket quality; capture and distribute follow-up actions.
  • Monitor workflow rules and automated notifications, support users with routine issues and training, and escalate system defects or sensitive cases.
  • Generate JIRA and ticketing reports that provide visibility into workload, status, bottlenecks, service levels and recurring issues

Job Governance, Job Descriptions and Data Integrity

  • Audit and maintain job profiles, job families, job descriptions, job catalog entries, job levels and personnel subareas in applicable systems.
  • Coordinate with Talent Acquisition and other HR partners to align job and compensation structures with approved salary structures, standards and new guidelines.
  • Review and update job descriptions across the organization and retrieve or share approved job descriptions upon request.
  • Research data discrepancies, complete routing and quality audits, and escalate unresolved governance or structural issues.

Audit, Compliance, Controls and Records

  • Gather, organize and validate data supporting incentive risk and compliance reviews, operational risk reviews and the Compensation Governance application.
  • Support periodic quality reviews, transaction sampling, documentation checks and audit-evidence preparation.
  • Maintain confidential, complete and current compensation records, trackers and shared-folder files in accordance with retention, access and file-handling controls.
  • Protect employee, salary, benefits and organizational information and promptly escalate control exceptions.


Systems, Testing and Performance-Process Support

  • Participate in ERP and HR-system testing, data validation, user training and system updates; serve as an operational liaison for Compensation systems.
  • Support performance-process administration by generating reports, coordinating movement of evaluation sheets, retrieving and distributing prior evaluations upon request, and uploading standardized objectives and ethics and compliance objectives.
  • Identify recurring issues and recommend improvements to workflows, rules, checklists, templates and controls.


Reporting, Process Documentation and Client Service

  • Maintain current data trackers, dashboard metrics and operational performance indicators that support management visibility and follow-up.
  • Coordinate cross-functional handoffs among Compensation, Talent Acquisition, Payroll, Our People Operations, HR partners and managers.
  • Maintain SOPs, process guides, job aids, templates and team files; standardize ticketing and operating practices across teams.
  • Provide responsive user service and clear procedural guidance, communicate status and missing requirements, and escalate urgent, unusual or policy-sensitive matters.


Special Projects and Other Duties

  • Support Compensation Governance, JIRA Service Management implementation, the Leader’s One Stop Shop, job-description audit work and other assigned process-improvement projects.
  • Perform other related duties and special assignments requested by the Compensation Supervisor.


MINIMUM EDUCATION


Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, Labor Relations, Office Systems or a related field. Equivalent relevant experience may be considered in accordance with organizational guidelines.

EXPERIENCE

  • One (1) to two (2) years of experience in Human Resources, HR operations, payroll, compensation, benefits administration, employee-data processing or a related operational function preferred.
  • Experience processing or validating employee transactions in SAP, SuccessFactors or another HRIS is strongly preferred.
  • Experience with JIRA or another case-management/ticketing platform and confidential employee or compensation information is preferred.


KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES

  • Strong attention to detail and ability to manage high-volume, date-sensitive transactions, cases and follow-up accurately.
  • Working knowledge of HR transactions, effective dates, employee and position data, service-level tracking and basic payroll-calendar dependencies.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Outlook, Word and Teams; ability to maintain trackers, validate data, prepare reports and use workflow systems.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, follow-up, troubleshooting and customer-service skills.
  • Ability to follow procedures, approval requirements, controls and escalation paths while handling confidential information with discretion and integrity.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills in English and Spanish preferred; ability to collaborate across functions within defined authority.

Important: The candidate must provide evidence of academic preparation or courses related to the job posting, if necessary.

title: Assistant Golf Professional
description:
West Bay Club, located in Estero, FL, is pleased to announce an excellent career opportunity for a Full-Time Assistant Golf Professional! We are seeking a driven individual who is eager to learn, contribute, and grow within a fast‑paced hospitality-focused property organization. As part of Troon, you’ll contribute to a global leader in golf and community management.
Annual Compensation: $57,200.00 BOE
West Bay Club - Estero, Florida
Nestled in the heart of Estero Bay, near the Gulf of Mexico, West Bay Club is a member-owned gated community and private golf club encompassing nearly 900 acres - 500 of which are dedicated to conservation. The community boasts 790 residences, including estate homes, high-rise condos, and villas, all set amidst lush tropical landscaping and bordering Estero Bay and Gulf of Mexico. West Bay recently underwent a $50 million renovation of the club amenities and golf course.
Located in the picturesque surroundings of West Bay’s community the Bay House facility includes a resort-style pool, state-of-the-art fitness center, spa, culinary academy, card and meeting rooms, and the Aqua Café offering both indoor and outdoor dining. West Bay’s tennis facility offers center court viewing on all eight Har-Tru courts. Additionally, the Sports Park offers six pickleball courts, two bocce courts, and a dog park. Residents also enjoy kayaking, canoeing, boating, and fishing all from the West Bay River Park's on-premises dock, featuring a private boat launch and boat storage.
A unique feature of the community is West Bay’s private Beach Club, which underwent a complete reconstruction, completed in March 2024. Residents enjoy direct access to their beachfront club along the Gulf of Mexico, complete with a full-service restaurant, valet service, and dedicated beach attendants providing beach service.
Within the community, the West Bay Golf Club is anchored around its 18-hole championship golf course. Designed by esteemed golf course architects Pete and PB Dye, renovated by Fry-Straka, golf enthusiasts seek out West Bay to experience its unique and challenging design. The Golf Club is home to multiple dining venues that range from casual dining, including the Niblick Grille and Signature Bar, to fine dining at the Golf House. The club offers a maximum of 300 golf memberships, 150 social memberships, and currently has a wait list. While the club remains open year-round, the peak of member activity is from November through April.
The Assistant Golf Professional is a key member of the golf operations team at the property and assists the 1st Assistant Golf Professional and/or Head Golf Professional in managing all golf and golf-related activities at the facility.
Qualifications, Knowledge and Skill Requirements:
  • 1-2 years golf industry experience preferred
  • College degree (PGM) preferred
  • PGA Member or Apprentice
  • Must have strong customer/guest orientation
  • Must have strong communication skills
  • Highly polished interpersonal skills, with the ability to connect with people easily and quickly
  • Must acquire basic computer skills
  • Must be dependable
Position Responsibilities:
  • Assist in managing facility and staff
  • Process customer reservations for guests of the golf course
  • Assist in coordinating of individual, group, and tournament play as directed by the 1st Assistant Golf Professional and/or Head Golf Professional
  • Assumes 1st Assistant golf professional’s duties in his or her absence
  • Produce daily reports related to rounds, sales, etc. for management
  • Works closely with Marshall and Starter to monitor all aspects of play including starting, monitoring pace of play, safety on the course and golf course markings
  • Provides customer service to arriving guests to help expedite check-in process
  • Perform other duties as assigned by supervisor or manager
Benefits & Other Compensation:
This position includes eligibility for the following benefits, subject to applicable plan terms:
  • Healthcare Benefits – Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage.
  • Retirement Benefits – 401(k) with employer match (19 years of age and older).
  • Time Off – Paid time off (PTO) and leaves of absence, in accordance with applicable law and eligibility criteria.
  • Additional Compensation – Eligible for Employee Meals
Eligibility for benefits and the specific terms, conditions, and offerings are governed by the applicable plan documents and company policies, which may be amended at the Company’s discretion.
This job description is not an exclusive or exhaustive list of all job functions that an associate in this position may be asked to perform from time to time.
About Troon Privé
Troon Privé is the private club division of Troon, the global leader in golf and club management. Dedicated exclusively to private clubs, Troon Privé partners with premier properties to deliver exceptional hospitality, personalized service, and outstanding member experiences. By combining industry-leading resources, expertise, and innovation with each club’s unique culture and traditions, Troon Privé helps create vibrant club communities where members, guests, and associates feel valued, welcomed, and connected. Our clubs are built on a commitment to service excellence, operational integrity, and creating memorable experiences that extend well beyond the golf course. Associates are empowered to grow their careers, develop their talents, and make a meaningful impact. Through a culture of collaboration, excellence, and continuous learning, our team members have the opportunity to be part of something special while helping shape the future of private club hospitality. Learn more at www.troon.com.

title: Senior Security Architect
description:
Who we are

We drive innovation, from advisory and implementation to managed services and beyond, powered by a global team of over 18,500 experts representing over 90 nations in more than 30 countries. With SAP at our core and a powerful ecosystem of partners such as Microsoft and ServiceNow, we continuously improve solutions and AI-driven technology to make them work for companies and their people.

As part of NTT DATA, a $30+ billion business and technology services, AI and digital infrastructure leader, we are connected to a truly global organization. As a Global Top Employer, NTT DATA serves 75% of the Fortune Global 100 and, with experts in over 70 countries, co-innovates solutions that encourage experimentation and recognize great work.

With us, you have endless opportunities to think big, act bold and take ownership. Make this the place where you belong, learn and build your network.

What you will be doing

  • As a Senior Security Architect, you will define and drive the security architecture for a global backup engineering capability protecting more than 450,000 virtual machines across multiple hyperscaler environments and supporting thousands of customers.
  • Your work will shape the security posture of a critical infrastructure capability, ensuring that backup and recovery systems remain resilient against evolving cyber threats and comply with demanding security and regulatory standards.
  • Define and drive the security architecture for enterprise backup and recovery solutions across AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, IBM Cloud and Alibaba Cloud.
  • Ensure that security designs align with organizational standards, industry frameworks and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Lead threat-modelling exercises, security assessments and vulnerability analyses for large-scale backup infrastructure.
  • Define and enforce identity and access management policies, role-based access control models, multi-factor authentication requirements and least-privilege principles.
  • Design and implement DevSecOps practices across CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code workflows and automated deployment processes.
  • Embed container security, infrastructure-as-code scanning and automated security testing into engineering workflows.
  • Collaborate with product management and engineering teams to integrate security requirements throughout the product development lifecycle.
  • Influence product roadmaps and feature priorities from a security-first perspective.
  • Develop and maintain ransomware and malware mitigation strategies for backup and recovery environments.
  • Define immutable backup designs, Zero Trust architectures, recovery strategies and incident response frameworks.
  • Integrate relevant threat intelligence into security controls, operational processes and response planning.
  • Contribute to internal and external security audit preparation, evidence gathering and stakeholder coordination.
  • Manage audit findings, remediation activities and continuous compliance improvements.
  • Conduct secure design and code reviews and provide actionable security guidance to engineering teams.
  • Monitor evolving threats, security practices and regulatory expectations and translate them into architecture improvements.

What you will bring along

  • A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Between 8 and 12 years of experience in information security, security architecture or a closely related field.
  • Deep DevSecOps expertise, including the integration of security into CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code scanning, container security and automated security testing.
  • A CISSP certification or an equivalent certification such as CISM or CCSP.
  • Strong working knowledge of recognized security frameworks, including NIST, ISO 27001 and CIS Controls.
  • Proven experience developing ransomware and malware mitigation strategies, including incident response planning, recovery design and threat intelligence integration.
  • Hands-on experience managing security audits, including preparation, evidence gathering, remediation tracking and stakeholder coordination.
  • Solid understanding of Zero Trust architecture principles and practical experience applying them to cloud and infrastructure environments.
  • Experience with Secure Software Development Lifecycle practices, including threat modelling, secure architecture and design reviews, and secure code reviews.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess complex risks and translate them into practical security controls.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence engineering, product and business teams.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a large-scale, international and multi-cloud environment.
  • Cloud security certifications would be considered a strong advantage, such as Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer, Microsoft Cybersecurity Architect Expert (SC-100), Azure Security
  • Engineer Associate (AZ-500), AWS Certified Security – Specialty or AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional.
  • Strong knowledge of AWS, Microsoft Azure or Google Cloud infrastructure, particularly compute, storage and networking services at scale, would be beneficial.
  • Experience securing cloud-native backup and disaster recovery solutions across multi-cloud environments would be an advantage.
  • Familiarity with SAP technologies, SAP infrastructure environments or SAP Business Technology Platform would be beneficial.
  • Experience contributing security perspectives to product roadmaps and feature prioritization would be advantageous.
  • Knowledge of container and Kubernetes security, including EKS, AKS or GKE, image scanning, runtime protection and orchestration hardening, would be beneficial.
  • You are fluent in written and spoken English.

Employment Type: Contract to Hire (CTH)

title: Research Scientist, AI Safety

Work closely with engineers to turn research designs into reproducible evaluations and share findings with outside research partners.

- Partner with engineers to produce reproducible environments with clear scoring and documented limitations.

- Write up results as benchmark releases, research reports and recommendations for partners.

Bonus points

- Experience evaluating models on AI R&D tasks, such as measuring models doing machine learning research or training models.

title: AI Solution Lead
description:
About BOI

BOI is the AI transformation studio that Walmart, Coca-Cola, and Mastercard call when AI needs to drive growth, not just savings. We bring together the unusually strong in frontier enterprise AI - then give them the ownership to make it happen. If you're looking for a comfortable place to hide, we're not it. If you want to build the future of enterprise AI with people who will make you better - welcome home.

About the Role

As AI Solution Lead, you own what we build for a client and make sure it lands. You start from the outcome the client needs, turn it into a solution roadmap, and run the project until it ships.

You work side by side with the engineering team. You find out what needs to be built and make sure it lives up to the client's expectations. You keep the client and the team pointed at the same outcome. You also help win the work. You join client conversations early, shape scope, and write the solution and delivery sections of proposals.

What You Will Do

Own the solution

You start from the business outcome and define the features that get there. You own the solution roadmap end-to-end and decide what ships first and what can wait. Along the way, you make sure the team builds what the client needs and push back when the work drifts from it.

Run delivery

You lead the weekly rhythm with the client and the team, from standups to steering committees. You own the client relationship, get their input into the build, and help land what engineering flags in terms the client acts on. You keep the project on time and on budget, spot risks early, and decide what escalates. And you make sure every person on the team knows their role.

Grow the business

You join pitches and scoping calls early and write the solution, roadmap, and delivery sections of proposals in collaboration with the engineering lead. Inside your projects, you spot follow-on work and raise it early. What you ship becomes case studies and reusable IP.

What We Screen For

We are deliberately not-for-everyone. We look for a specific combination of qualities:

  • Low ego. You're confident and grounded. You own mistakes, invite critique, and share credit.
  • High aptitude. You get to the core of a messy problem fast and explain it simply.
  • High ownership. You move things forward without waiting to be told, even when the brief is unclear.
  • Delivery track record. You've led digital or AI projects from scope to launch, with real clients, deadlines, and budgets. Typically 4+ years in solution, product, or delivery roles, ideally with pre-sales experience.
  • Technically literate. You've worked closely with engineering teams on AI or data products. You know how LLM apps, RAG, and agents fit together and where they break. You don't write production code.
  • Commercially aware. You know what makes a scope credible to a buyer and a project profitable to run.
  • A point of view on AI. You use it daily. You've thought past the demo, to what it changes for the people whose work it touches.

What We Offer

  • Get ahead, stay ahead - build compounding skills at the frontier of AI, while others are still catching up
  • First of a kind work - the world's most pioneering AI transformation projects, not PowerPoint recycling
  • Freedom to explore - prototype, experiment, and push boundaries on what's possible with AI
  • Shape the business - not just deliver projects, but help build a growing company like an owner
  • A team you'll enjoy - creative, ambitious, supportive, and never boring
  • Competitive package - solid perks, delicious office lunches, and regular team gatherings

BOI is an equal opportunity employer: we celebrate diversity and welcome all backgrounds and identities.

We do not accept candidates submitted by agencies.

description:

Large-scale SAP S/4HANA Cloud rollout program, covering complex integrations between SAP S/4HANA and SAP/non-SAP applications across an international environment.

title: Assistant Manager - Training
description:

Training & Learning Support

Communication Management

  • Support the development and execution of internal communication plans and initiatives.
  • Coordinate communication activities across various communication channels and platforms.
  • Draft, review, and distribute communication materials, including announcements, newsletters, presentations, notices, and promotional content.
  • Ensure communication materials are accurate, consistent, and aligned with corporate communication standards and branding guidelines.
  • Support leadership and stakeholder communication initiatives as required.

Change Management & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Support organizational change and transformation initiatives through training and communication activities.
  • Assist in the preparation and implementation of change communication plans, learning interventions, and awareness campaigns.
  • Coordinate stakeholder engagement activities, workshops, briefings, and feedback sessions.
  • Monitor employee feedback and communication effectiveness to support successful adoption of new initiatives.
  • Collaborate with project teams and business functions to address communication and training requirements.

Knowledge Management & Continuous Improvement

  • Assist in maintaining knowledge repositories, communication resources, and learning materials.
  • Support the development and implementation of training and communication standards, templates, and guidelines.
  • Identify opportunities to enhance training effectiveness, communication reach, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Conduct research on industry trends, best practices, and emerging tools relating to learning and communication.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that support organizational capability development and employee awareness.

Governance & Administration

  • Ensure training and communication activities comply with Company policies, procedures, and governance requirements.
  • Maintain accurate records, reports, and supporting documentation for training and communication programmes.
  • Support audits, reviews, compliance assessments, and reporting requirements as required.
  • Assist in tracking budgets, vendor invoices, and programme-related expenditures where applicable.

Primary Responsibility

The Assistant Manager, Training & Communication is responsible for supporting the development, implementation, and administration of enterprise-wide training, learning, and communication initiatives that enhance organizational effectiveness, employee engagement, and business performance.

The incumbent collaborates with stakeholders across the organization to coordinate training programmes, communication activities, change initiatives, and knowledge-sharing efforts to ensure consistent messaging, employee awareness, and capability development.

The role assists in the execution of training and communication strategies, monitors programme effectiveness, and supports continuous improvement initiatives to strengthen organizational learning and communication outcomes.

Requirements

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's Degree in Communications, Business Administration, Human Resources, Education, Organizational Development, Marketing, Public Relations, or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in training, learning and development, communications, organizational development, employee engagement, or a related field.
  • Experience in coordinating training programmes, communication campaigns, or change initiatives.
  • Experience working with cross-functional stakeholders and supporting enterprise-wide initiatives.
  • Experience in a large corporate environment would be an advantage.

Knowledge & Skills

  • Good knowledge of learning and development, training administration, and communication practices.
  • Strong written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Good project coordination and organizational skills.
  • Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building abilities.
  • Good analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and communication or learning management platforms.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality.

title: Club Manager and GM
description:
THE OASIS CLUB, located in CHAMPIONSGATE, FL, is pleased to announce an excellent career opportunity for Club Manager! We are seeking a motivated individual who is interested in contributing to a positive experience for our members and guests while continuing to grow their knowledge of golf club operations. As an associate of Troon, you’ll contribute to a global leader in golf and community management.

Manages all aspects of the Club including its activities and the relationships between the Club, Troon Golf, Ownership group, and/or the Board of Directors, members, guests, associates, community, government and industry.

Essential Duties:

  • Administers Club policies and procedures established by the Board of Directors and/or Ownership group.
  • Plans, develops and approves specific operational policies, programs, procedures and methods in concert with general policies.
  • Monitors monthly and other financial reports/statements on a daily, weekly and monthly basis for the facility and takes effective corrective action when necessary.
  • Coordinates the development of the Club’s long-range and annual (business) plans.
  • Works with Troon Golf Human Resources Department to establish a basic personnel policy; initiate and monitor policies relating to personnel actions and training and professional development programs.
  • Responsible for interviewing, hiring, training, planning, assigning, and directing work, evaluating performance, rewarding, and disciplining associates; addressing complaints and resolving problems.
  • Directly manages department members that may include, but is not limited to: Assistant General Manager (Clubhouse Manager); Food and Beverage Director; Membership Director; Golf Professional; Superintendent; Tennis Professional; Athletic Club Manager; Administrative Assistant.
  • Attends conferences, workshops and meetings to keep abreast of current information and developments in the field.
  • Coordinates development of operating and capital budgets according to the budget calendar; monitors monthly and other financial statements for the Club; takes effective corrective action as required.
  • Coordinates and serves as ex-officio member of the Board of Directors and other appropriate Club standing committees.
  • Provides advice and recommendations to the President and committees about construction, alterations, maintenance, materials, supplies, equipment and services not provided in approved plans and/or budgets.
  • Consistently ensures that the Club is operated in accordance with all applicable local, state and federal laws.
  • Oversees the care and maintenance of all the Club’s physical assets and facilities.
  • Ensures the highest standards for food, beverage, sports and recreation, entertainment and other Club services.
  • Establishes and monitors compliance with Troon Golf Procurement purchasing policies and procedures.
  • Participates in outside activities that are judged as appropriate and approved by the Board of Directors/Ownership group to enhance the prestige of the Club; broadens the scope of the Club’s operation by fulfilling the public obligations of the Club as a participating member of the community.
  • Reports member infractions to the Board of Directors/Ownership group for necessary action.
  • Serves as liaison between all management staff and the Board of Directors.
  • Maintains relations with police, fire, liquor control board, health department and other governmental agencies.
  • Performs competitive analyses on Clubs and other businesses providing member alternatives through personal observations and historical reports.
  • Handles emergencies such as fires, accidents and breaches of security or house rules promptly and in person. Emphasizes prevention through training, inspection and preventive enforcement.
  • Convenes and presides over meetings with departmental managers; conducts all-facility personnel meetings.
  • Gives direction to and works closely with vendors, outside contractors, firms and individuals providing services, lease agreements, or contracts to the Club.
  • This job description is not an exclusive or exhaustive list of all job functions that an associate in this position may be asked to perform from time to time.

Education/Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree (BA); or four to six years related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience. (Multi-course facilities may require more experience.)

Physical Demands:

  • Regularly stands, walks and sits. Occasionally may climbs, balances, stoops, kneels, crawls, crouches, tastes or smells. Regularly uses hands to finger, feel or handle, reaches with arms and hands, talks or hears. Occasionally lifts up to 50 pounds.

Environment/Noise:

  • Occasionally works in outdoor weather conditions. Noise level is moderate.

Certificates/Licenses:

  • Food Manager Certification

Job Knowledge, Skill, and Ability Preferences:

  • Ability to read and speak English may be required in order to perform the duties of the job (e.g. the associates may be required to communicate with English speaking customers or co-workers, the manuals for the equipment the associates may use are in English).
  • Knowledge of Microsoft Office applications.

This job description is not an exclusive or exhaustive list of all job functions that an associate in this position may be asked to perform from time to time.

Benefits & Other Compensation:
This position includes eligibility for the following benefits, subject to applicable plan terms:

  • Healthcare Benefits – Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage
  • Retirement Benefits – 401(k) with employer match (19 years of age and older)
  • Time Off – Paid time off (PTO) and leaves of absence, in accordance with applicable law and eligibility criteria

Eligibility for benefits and the specific terms, conditions, and offerings are governed by the applicable plan of documents and company policies, which may be amended at the Company’s discretion.
